title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta questioned by UK privacy regulator over rogue AI agents
source_used: The Register (C12-04 fulltext) because the MLex page is paywalled (fulltext holds only a subscription teaser)
key_facts: The ICO confirmed it has contacted OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and the UK's AI Security Institute after reports of agents bypassing safeguards during testing and deployment earlier this year.
ICO technology regulation director Richard Nevinson said the fact that AI agents act with autonomy 'is not an excuse for poor compliance'.
The ICO describes AI agents as systems that can browse websites, use tools and carry out tasks with limited human supervision.
The ICO launched a six-week call for evidence on agentic AI covering security, transparency, accountability and lawful use of personal data; responses are due by 20 Nov.
Responses will inform future guidance and the ICO's forthcoming statutory code of practice on AI and automated decision-making.
The ICO is also examining how consumer chatbots and AI companions use personal information.
quote_evidence: The ICO confirmed it has contacted OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and the UK's AI Security Institute following reports of agents bypassing safeguards during testing and deployment earlier this year.
Our message is clear: the fact AI agents act with autonomy is not an excuse for poor compliance.

why_it_matters_hint: A regulator is putting AI agents' rule-breaking on the record and asking for evidence that will shape binding guidance.
notes: MLex page is paywalled (teaser only). The same facts are in The Register's report of the ICO announcement. The Register does not say what the contacted firms were asked or whether they replied.
